claims.text: The starting coatings are nanoscale multilayers containing mixed FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy phases.
The starting multilayers inherently contain severe lattice distortion.
The starting multilayers contain localized chemical short-range order.
The creep mechanism in a high-entropy alloy can vary with loading rate.
Increasing loading rate causes FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers to transition from diffusion-controlled creep to dislocation-mediated creep.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneity, severe lattice distortion, and chemical short-range order drive the proposed creep-mechanism transition.
Nanoindentation is suitable for evaluating creep at small length scales.
Systematically varying nanoindentation loading rate while retaining the multilayer architecture provides the proposed controlled comparison.
Ambient-temperature loading-rate variation can trigger creep behavior without compromising the nanoscale multilayer structure.
Chemical short-range order and severe lattice distortion differentially affect atom-vacancy exchange and dislocation nucleation.
At lower loading rates, creep is dominated by direct atom-vacancy exchange in highly lattice-distorted regions.
Increasing the loading rate reduces the activation barrier for dislocation nucleation.
Increasing the loading rate enhances dislocation nucleation and glide.
A low creep stress exponent is indicative of diffusion-controlled creep.
Increasing loading rate will increase the creep stress exponent relative to the low-rate baseline.
Increasing loading rate will produce more observable dislocation activity than the low-rate baseline.
At the low-loading-rate baseline, creep is primarily diffusion-based and dislocation-mediated plasticity is minimal.
The proposed behavior is limited to conditions in which the multilayer nanoarchitecture remains intact and catastrophic failure does not occur.
TEM can be used to compare dislocation activity across loading rates, while creep stress exponents provide a complementary mechanical indicator.
Failure to observe either an increased creep stress exponent or a shift toward greater dislocation activity with increasing loading rate would falsify the hypothesis.
